sources.citation: Lohmann, Roger Ivar. Trent University faculty profile and Curriculum Vitae (web pages, downloaded 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Nothing. Profile states fieldnotes and recordings of the Asaba language 'are being systematically organized in preparation for an initial dictionary and grammar of this language spoken by about 200 people'; CV lists no linguistic publication on Asaba (all works ethnographic).

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Suarmin language' and Glottolog 5.x languoid page suar1238 (read online 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Nothing; no phonology section; Glottolog lists zero grammar/phonology/sketch references (Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist).

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; sec. 2.4.2 Asaba [seo] (p.186) and Table 1 give documentation status as 'Short wordlist', with 'some very brief notes on grammar in Laycock & Z'Graggen 1975' and anthropological studies (Lohmann 2000; Little 2008). Confirms no phonological description exists as of 2010.

sources.citation: Steer, Martin. 2005. Languages of the Upper Sepik and Central New Guinea. Report prepared for the Upper Sepik-Central New Guinea Project (edits and Appendix 9.2 by B. Craig 2011). South Australian Museum / USCNGP. 60 pp.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content on Asaba/Duranmin: 'Neighbouring languages are the Ok family (south and west), Duranmin (north-west), the Sepik Hill family..' is the only mention.
sources.venue: Report prepared for the Upper Sepik-Central New Guinea Project (edits and Appendix 9.2 on verification

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 2001. Language endangerment in the insular Greater Pacific area, and the New Guinea area in particular. In A. Pawley, M. Ross & D. Tryon (eds), The boy from Bundaberg: Studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton (Pacific Linguistics 514), 383-398. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. hdl:1885/254068
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content; endangerment-status table entry only: 'Duranmin (Suarmin) P 100 SDP'.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Ronald K. Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 243-273. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. p.248: Duranmin ('also occasionally called Wani'), 141 speakers in Siliam and Siliambil, classified as isolate (max 6% shared cognates), shared animate suffix -pu/-po/-fo; p.252 sociolinguistic notes (Telefol bilingualism). Wordlists only; no suprasegmental information.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76)

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & T. Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-35. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical survey; Duranmin appears only p.13 sec.3.6 ('Paupe.. is 29% cognate with Duranmin, a language spoken in a few hamlets on the Kenu River') and in wordlist tables. Phonology summaries in the paper concern Arai and Upper Sepik stock languages, not Duranmin.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40)

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. & John A. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 731-764.
sources.note: Nothing. p.753 adds Duranmin to the Leonhard Schultze sub-phylum on Conrad & Dye's 29% figure; the 'very brief notes on grammar' concern noun classification in Pai/Walio/Papi, not Duranmin phonology.
sources.venue: New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification (Pacific Linguistics B-25). Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing; Duranmin and Suarmin appear only as village names listed under 204 Oksapmin.
